digest.component_or_area: workflow subsystem — step registry, seam tests, and module size guards
propositions: Three seam-test guards are needed to defend against module regrowth: headroom for unguarded hot files, a stale guard assertion that must name the correct call-site locations, and a registry-membership assertion that catches missed registration imports.

Workflow steps register via @register_step as an import side effect into process-global STEP_REGISTRY; a missed registration import (e.g. deleting prerequisite_workflow_ops import at workflow_ops.py:45) is invisible to the schema linter and to test_contracts.py because both work only on already-populated registry state.

The registry-membership and gate-YAML-resolution guards must run in subprocess isolation with clean sys.modules to observe first-import registration; an in-process check remains green even when registration imports are deleted because prior test modules have already populated the registry.

Headroom assertions for plan_review/workflow_ops.py (794 LOC) and llm/config.py (793 LOC) must be staged at < 800 now; sibling extraction tickets will tighten each to < 700 once refactoring creates headroom, keeping every ticket independently landable.

test_gate_dispatch_seam.py's assertion message incorrectly claims gate_dispatch.py holds three finalize_verdict call sites; it holds zero; the sites now live in plan_review_recovery.py (3) and plan_review/workflow_ops.py (2) after Change 1484 moved them.

An unregistered or stale workflow step cannot be caught statically by any existing layer (schema treats uses as free-form string, linter skips unknown steps, test_contracts.py only iterates present registry); a guard catching the defect at first import is the only structural defence.
